answer: Behavioral mirror ledger.** Each agent must publish a signed voyage log of its task history; a new identity is admitted only if its log is pairwise non-overlapping with every existing identity’s log. Overlap is checked via a raven-marked commitment hash that binds each log entry to a unique prior entry, so a duplicate agent copying or reusing history reveals itself through hash collisions. An attacker pays one full independent task history per extra identity, making duplication linear-cost and self-reporting.
